families.title: Motif transformations
families.intro: One short cell, many statements: the listener tracks identity through change. Every transformation keeps one property (rhythm, contour, intervals) and changes another.

families.title: Interplay
families.intro: How two or more lines share time and register: who speaks, who answers, who holds.

families.title: Cross-textural development
families.intro: The same idea travels between instruments, registers and domains (pitch to rhythm, synth to voice), so a long track stays one piece.

families.title: Foreshadowing
families.intro: Plant early, pay later: partial statements before the hook, the full hook at the drop, a callback at the end.

families.title: Layering and density
families.intro: How many things sound at once, in which roles and frequency slots, and how a loop evolves on each repeat.

families.title: Tension and release
families.intro: The grammar of expectation: harmonic, rhythmic, spectral and dynamic tension, and where it lands.

families.title: Energy curves
families.intro: The macro shape of a track: energy per section and the ramps inside a phrase.

families.title: Transitions and dovetails
families.intro: How one section hands over to the next (docs/CONVENTIONS.md section 6 holds the shipped dt. atoms).

families.title: Groove and feel
families.intro: Rhythm sequence archetypes and micro-timing: swing, push and pull, ghost notes, polymeter (docs/CONVENTIONS.md sections 4-5).

families.title: Harmonic design
families.intro: Chord loops, voice leading, pedals and harmonic rhythm.

families.title: Tone borrowing
families.intro: Borrow pitch material from a parallel mode or key, or timbre, envelope and groove from another layer or genre.

families.title: Discordance
families.intro: Intentional clashes (minor seconds, tritones, clusters, beating unisons) placed where tension is the point, and resolved on purpose.

families.title: Assonance and consonance
families.intro: Sound-similarity that binds layers: shared formants, harmonic series, colours, rhythm cells and envelopes.

families.title: Complementing
families.intro: One layer fills the gaps of another: in frequency, time, stereo, length and dynamics.

families.title: Synergy
families.intro: Pairs that only work together: the sum is a new sound, not two sounds.

families.title: Clustering
families.intro: Tone clusters, rhythmic clusters, event bursts in time, and clustering as analysis (bars, motifs).

families.title: Sound-design layering
families.intro: One instrument from several layers: sub, body, bite, air; parallel and serial processing.

families.title: Vocal as instrument
families.intro: Pitched syllables, vowels and formant pads; no lyrics are written or implied.

families.title: Arrangement maps
families.intro: Section maps per genre as gates and masks, so a track is one program with selections, not copies.

sections.title: MOT-01 Transposition
sections.explain: The whole cell moved up or down by a fixed interval; intervals and rhythm are kept.
notes: Interval and rhythm patterns are what memory encodes for a melody (contour plus interval), so the cell is recognised at a new pitch; a new register also changes brightness and the chord it sits on.
Second half of a 16-bar phrase, a lift into the last drop, answering phrases.
composer ledger: relation "transposed" (or "octave") to the first statement, with the semitone offset.
Transposing every repeat (the listener loses the home pitch)
Chromatic transposition that leaves the key by accident (check composer discord, out-of-key share)

sections.title: MOT-02 Sequence
sections.explain: A transposition repeated in steps in consecutive windows (a chain: up a step, up a step).
notes: Predictable stepwise displacement creates momentum: the ear extrapolates the next step and the arrival on a stable degree releases it.
Builds, pre-drops, bridges; two or three links, then break the chain.
composer ledger: relation "sequence" (transposed repeat in the next window of the same layer).
Sequences longer than 3-4 links (a predictable rosalia tires fast)
Sequencing every layer in parallel (all motion, no anchor)

sections.title: MOT-03 Inversion
sections.explain: Each interval flips direction (up a third becomes down a third), tonally inside the scale.
notes: Contour is the strongest melodic cue; flipping it keeps rhythm and interval sizes, so the cell is related yet heard as an answer.
Response phrases, second verse or second drop, counterlines against the original.
Inverting a cell whose identity is its rhythm only (no audible change)
Real (chromatic) inversion that leaves the key

examples.title: MOT-03 inversion
examples.code:
atom("m", { type: "mini", body: "0 2 4 3" })
atom("mInv", { type: "mini", body: "0 -2 -4 -3" })
$: n(atoms.m).scale("C4:minor").s("triangle").hook("hygiene-lead")
$: n(atoms.mInv).scale("C4:minor").s("triangle").hook("hygiene-lead").late(1)

sections.title: MOT-04 Retrograde and retro-inversion
sections.explain: The pitches (and optionally the rhythm) played backwards; retro-inversion also flips intervals.
notes: A weaker relation than transposition (memory is forward), so it reads as new material with a family resemblance; good for development sections that must not sound like the hook.
Expecting listeners to recognise retrograde of a long line (only short cells survive)

sections.title: MOT-05 Augmentation and diminution
sections.explain: Note values doubled (augmentation) or halved (diminution); pitches kept.
notes: Time-scaling keeps contour and intervals; augmentation reads as weight and calm, diminution as urgency. In half-time genres augmentation turns a drop riff into a pad line.
Augment for intros, breakdowns and outro callbacks; diminish in builds and fills.
Diminution past the 1/16 grid at club tempos (smear)
Augmenting into sustained notes that mask the vocal band

sections.title: MOT-06 Fragmentation
sections.explain: A piece of the cell (usually its head or tail) repeated on its own.
notes: The fragment is cheap to recognise and leaves room; repetition of a fragment builds expectation for the whole.
Teasers (FS-01), builds (shorter and shorter fragments), fills.
composer ledger: relation "fragment" (a contiguous piece of >= 3 notes).
Fragments of a cell that has not yet been established and will never come (no payoff)

sections.title: MOT-07 Extension
sections.explain: The cell continues past its end with new notes (an answer tail), often to reach a cadence.
notes: The head keeps identity, the tail adds direction; ending on a stable degree gives closure.
The 4th bar of a 4-bar phrase, phrase endings before section changes.
composer ledger: relation "extension" or a motif "grown from" the first (grown_from).
Tails that never resolve (no cadence anywhere in the track)

examples.title: MOT-07 extension
examples.code:
atom("m", { type: "mini", body: "0 2 4 3" })
atom("tail", { type: "mini", body: "2 1 0 -1" })
$: n(cat(atoms.m, atoms.m, atoms.m, atoms.tail)).scale("C4:minor").s("sawtooth").hook("hygiene-lead").lpf(2000)

sections.title: MOT-08 Rhythmic displacement
sections.explain: The same cell starting at a different point of the bar (an eighth or a beat later).
notes: Metric position changes accent: the same notes against the grid make new syncopation (rhythmic dissonance) without new material.
Second half of a drop, switch-ups, tension before a downbeat.
composer ledger: relation "displaced" (same intervals and rhythm, shifted start); composer feel: syncopation index rises.
Displacing the kick or the bass root (the floor loses the one)

sections.title: MOT-09 Interval expansion and compression
sections.explain: Same contour and rhythm, wider or narrower steps.
notes: Contour identity holds while range changes energy: expansion opens (lift), compression tightens (tension, chromatic menace).
Expand in the last drop; compress in builds and dark breakdowns.
composer ledger: relation "expanded" / "compressed" (same contour, larger / smaller interval sum).
Expansion past an octave in a lead that must sit in the vocal band

examples.title: MOT-09 interval expansion and compression
examples.code:
atom("m", { type: "mini", body: "0 2 4 3" })
atom("mWide", { type: "mini", body: "0 4 7 5" })
$: n("<0 1>").pick([atoms.m, atoms.mWide]).scale("C4:minor").s("sawtooth").hook("hygiene-lead")

sections.title: MOT-10 Reharmonization
sections.explain: The melody kept, the chords under it changed (relative minor, borrowed chord, new bass note).
notes: The same melody note gets a new function (root, third, ninth): its colour and stability change while the tune is recognised.
Last chorus or drop, breakdowns (sentimental lift), outros.
composer discord: chord roots per bar change while composer ledger keeps the melody "exact".
Reharmonising under a vocal hook without checking clashes (minor 2nds against held melody notes)

examples.title: MOT-10 reharmonization
examples.code:
$: n("0 2 4 3").scale("C4:minor").s("triangle").hook("hygiene-lead")
$: chord("<Cm Cm Ab Ab Fm Fm G G>/2").voicing().s("supersaw").hook("hygiene-pad").gain(0.25)
examples.lowered:
$: n("0 2 4 3").scale("C4:minor").s("triangle").hpf(150).lpf(8000)
$: chord("<Cm Cm Ab Ab Fm Fm G G>/2").voicing().s("supersaw").hpf(180).lpf(6000).gain(0.25)

sections.title: MOT-11 Ornament
sections.explain: Extra notes around the cell: grace notes, turns, trills, ghosted repeats; the cell notes stay on their steps.
notes: Adds detail on repeats without changing identity; the ear hears the frame plus decoration.
Embellishment ladder (LAY-05): the 3rd and 4th repeat of a loop.
Ornaments on every note (the frame disappears)
Grace notes on the bass at low frequencies (mud)

sections.title: INT-01 Call and response
sections.explain: One phrase asks, another answers, in alternating time slots.
notes: Turn-taking keeps each voice audible (no masking in time) and sets up a predictable cycle that can then be broken.
Riddim and dubstep bass phrases (A/B basses), lead vs vocal chop, hook sections.
composer layers: high onset_complement between the two lanes and composer ledger shows the answer as a related motif (inverted, transposed).
Answer louder or busier than the call every time (no hierarchy)
Both voices in the same band (they still mask across the seam)

sections.title: INT-02 Counterline
sections.explain: A second melody that moves against the first: contrary or oblique motion, notes in the first line's rests.
notes: Independent contour (contrary motion) is heard as a separate stream (auditory stream segregation); filling rests adds detail without masking.
Second half of drops, relief sections, last chorus.
engine/motifs counterlines (contrary/oblique share); composer layers onset_complement > 0.7.
Parallel fifths/octaves for long stretches (fuses into one stream)
A counterline in the same register as the vocal

sections.title: INT-03 Hocket
sections.explain: One line split note by note between two voices or timbres.
notes: The ear fuses the line (pitch proximity) while the timbre alternation adds motion and stereo interest.
Plucks and bells in breakdowns; stereo ping-pong leads.
composer layers: onset_complement close to 1 and rhythm_rhyme close to 0 for the pair; pan_contrast > 0.4.
Hocketing across very different registers (the line breaks into two streams)

examples.title: INT-03 hocket
examples.code:
$: n("0 2 4 3 2 4 5 4").scale("C4:minor").s("triangle").hook("hygiene-pluck").struct("x ~ x ~ x ~ x ~").pan(0.2)
$: n("0 2 4 3 2 4 5 4").scale("C4:minor").s("square").hook("hygiene-pluck").struct("~ x ~ x ~ x ~ x").pan(0.8).gain(0.4)
examples.lowered:
$: n("0 2 4 3 2 4 5 4").scale("C4:minor").s("triangle").hpf(120).lpf(7000).struct("x ~ x ~ x ~ x ~").pan(0.2)
$: n("0 2 4 3 2 4 5 4").scale("C4:minor").s("square").hpf(120).lpf(7000).struct("~ x ~ x ~ x ~ x").pan(0.8).gain(0.4)

sections.title: INT-04 Handoff (relay)
sections.explain: The motif passes from one instrument to another at a section or phrase boundary.
notes: Continuity of material with a change of colour: the listener follows the motif, so the arrangement can change around it.
Section changes (lead to pluck at the breakdown, pluck to vocal at the hook).
composer ledger: the motif lists both layers in migration order with no gap bar between them.
Handoff with an empty bar in between (the thread drops)

sections.title: INT-05 Unison and octave doubling
sections.explain: Two timbres play the same line at the same pitch or octaves apart.
notes: Partials of both sounds fuse into one richer timbre (common fate); the octave adds brightness without a new line.
Drops (lead + supersaw octave), bass + sub doubling, emphasis on a hook bar.
composer layers (stems): synergy lufs_gain_db > 0 (coherent), assonance mfcc_cosine high; composer ledger relation "octave".
Doubling with slight detune at low pitch (beating in the sub, see DIS-03)
Doubling everything (density with no new information)

sections.title: INT-06 Imitation and canon
sections.explain: A second voice repeats the first after a delay, at the same or another pitch.
notes: The echo creates a predictable texture of overlapping copies (delay lines are acoustic canons); at a fifth it implies harmony.
Arps, plucks, ambient intros; DnB and progressive layers.
composer ledger: the same motif in two layers (or one) with "transposed" / "displaced" relations a fixed delay apart.

sections.title: INT-07 Pedal and ostinato under melody
sections.explain: A held or repeated bass note (pedal) or riff (ostinato) while the melody and chords move.
notes: A fixed reference makes harmonic motion above it audible as tension (non-chord tones against the pedal) and gives trance-like continuity.
Intros, builds (dominant pedal), phonk and techno grooves.
composer discord: roughness rises when upper chords leave the pedal and falls on return; engine/motifs chord loop over one bass root.
A pedal under a chord that clashes for many bars without resolution (check unresolved clashes)

examples.title: INT-07 pedal and ostinato under melody

sections.title: XT-01 Motif migration
sections.explain: The motif is stated by different layers over the track: bass, then lead, pluck, vocal syllable, pad, percussion rhythm.
notes: One idea in many colours gives unity with variety; each new texture is a new event even though no new material is added.
Long tracks (3+ minutes), extended mixes, any track whose sections risk sounding unrelated.
composer ledger: one motif with 3+ layers in its migration list.
Migration with a different motif in each layer (no thread)
Every layer stating the motif at once (no migration, only doubling)

examples.title: XT-01 motif migration
examples.code:
atom("m", { type: "mini", body: "0 2 4 3" })
atom("one", { type: "mini", body: "<1 0 0 0>" })
atom("two", { type: "mini", body: "<0 1 0 0>" })
atom("three", { type: "mini", body: "<0 0 1 0>" })
$: n(atoms.m).scale("C2:minor").s("sawtooth").hook("hygiene-bass").mask(atoms.one)
$: n(atoms.m).scale("C4:minor").s("sawtooth").hook("hygiene-lead").mask(atoms.two)
$: n(atoms.m).scale("C5:minor").s("triangle").hook("hygiene-pluck").mask(atoms.three)

sections.title: XT-02 Timbral morphing
sections.explain: The same notes, with the timbre changing over time (filter, vowel, waveform, FM index).
notes: Timbre is a separate perceptual dimension: a slow change of spectral centroid reads as development and energy without new pitches.
composer scan: spectral centroid / band map changes per bar while composer ledger reports "exact" statements.
Morphing that ends where it began with no arrival
Morphing several layers in sync (one wash)

sections.title: XT-03 Rhythm from pitch
sections.explain: The motif's rhythm alone, played on an unpitched layer (rim, hat, noise).
notes: Rhythm is a strong identity cue; the percussion echo keeps the motif present while the melody rests, and builds anticipation.
Builds and intros before the hook (FS-01), breakdowns.
composer ledger: rhythm_echoes lists the motif and the unpitched layer.
A rhythm echo that is an even grid (carries no identity)

examples.title: XT-03 rhythm from pitch
examples.code:
atom("mr", { type: "mini", body: "x ~ x x ~ x ~ ~" })
$: n("0 ~ 2 4 ~ 3 ~ ~").scale("C4:minor").s("triangle").hook("hygiene-lead").mask("<0 1>")
$: s("white").struct(atoms.mr).decay(0.04).hpf(4000).gain(0.4).mask("<1 0>")

sections.title: XT-04 Pitch from rhythm
sections.explain: A drum or percussion rhythm becomes a melodic line (the hat accents become pluck notes).
notes: Binding melody to the groove makes them lock (shared onsets); the melody feels inevitable.
Drops, especially percussion-led genres (electro, hyphy, riddim).
composer layers: rhythm_rhyme close to 1 between the drum lane and the melodic lane.
Copying a dense hat pattern into a melody (too many notes)

examples.title: XT-04 pitch from rhythm
examples.code:
atom("hatAcc", { type: "mini", body: "x ~ ~ x ~ ~ x ~" })
$: s("white").struct(atoms.hatAcc).decay(0.03).hpf(6000).gain(0.4)
$: n("0 3 5").scale("C4:minor").struct(atoms.hatAcc).s("triangle").hook("hygiene-pluck")
examples.lowered:
$: s("white").struct("x ~ ~ x ~ ~ x ~").decay(0.03).hpf(6000).gain(0.4)
$: n("0 3 5").scale("C4:minor").struct("x ~ ~ x ~ ~ x ~").s("triangle").hpf(120).lpf(7000)

sections.title: XT-05 Motif as vocal syllable
sections.explain: The motif sung on vowels or syllables (no words), or a synthetic vowel playing its pitches.
notes: Voice-like formants grab attention (speech sensitivity) and make a synth motif feel human at the hook.
Hooks and drops of melodic genres; phonk vocal chops; breakdowns.
composer layers: shared vowel with another layer (ASN-01); composer ledger: motif in the vox lane.
Writing lyrics into the user's track (never infer words)
Vowel filters on a sub-bass fundamental (formants sit above 300 Hz)

sections.title: FS-01 Pre-echo teaser
sections.explain: A fragment or the rhythm of the drop hook in the intro or build.
notes: Exposure creates familiarity; the full statement later is then recognised and rewarding (mere exposure, expectation).
composer foreshadow: pre_echo PASS (fragment, filtered or rhythm echo before the first drop).
The full hook at full level in the intro (payoff given away, see FS-04)

sections.title: FS-02 Filtered, reversed or sparse preview
sections.explain: The hook itself, low-passed, reversed or thinned (degraded), before the drop.
notes: Removing brightness or notes keeps identity at lower salience: the listener half-hears it, and the drop "opens" it.
Builds (opening filter), the bar before the drop (reversed), intros.
composer foreshadow: teasers marked "filtered" (lpf < 2 kHz or level < 0.6 x drop); composer scan band map: highs absent before the drop.
A filter so closed the teaser is inaudible (no exposure)

examples.title: FS-02 filtered, reversed or sparse preview

sections.title: FS-03 Planted harmony
sections.explain: The drop's chord loop sounds early (pad, bass pedal) before the hook melody arrives.
notes: The harmonic frame primes the key and the melody's target notes; the hook then lands on expected ground.
Intros and breakdowns that lead into a drop.
composer foreshadow: planted_harmony PASS (drop pitch-class sets found before the first drop).
New chords only at the drop (the hook arrives on unknown ground)

sections.title: FS-04 Delayed payoff
sections.explain: The full, bright, same-layer statement of the hook is withheld until the drop (or a later drop).
notes: Anticipation is the source of the reward response; withholding the expected event raises its value when it lands.
Every drop-based form; second drops can withhold one more layer.
composer foreshadow: withheld PASS (no full unfiltered same-layer statement before the first drop).
Withholding so long the hook never fully arrives
Revealing it in bar 1 of the intro

examples.title: FS-04 delayed payoff
examples.code:
atom("pay", { type: "gate", body: "@3b" })
hooks.bind("open", [["lpf", 6000]], atoms.pay)
hooks.bind("open", [["lpf", 600]], "<3b")
$: n("0 2 4 3").scale("C4:minor").s("sawtooth").hook("hygiene-lead").use("open")
examples.lowered_note: the binding is gated (it opens at a bar or in a range): gates are evaluated by the Craft runtime as the song plays, plain Strudel has no timeline of bindings

sections.title: FS-05 Callback and outro return
sections.explain: The hook (or its seed) returns after the last drop: augmented, filtered or on another layer.
notes: Return closes the form (rounded binary logic); the listener leaves with the hook in memory.
composer foreshadow: callback PASS (a statement after the last drop or in the last section).
An outro of new material that never returns to the hook

sections.title: FS-06 Return after contrast
sections.explain: After a contrasting section (breakdown, bridge) the motif returns, often varied (MOT family).
notes: Contrast resets habituation, so the return feels fresh; variation on return signals progress.
composer ledger: the motif is not flagged "never returns"; a gap of >= 4 bars precedes a later statement.
Motifs stated in one section only (ledger flag "never returns")

sections.title: LAY-01 Detail budget per section
sections.explain: Plan how many events and layers each section may have, from the energy curve (EN-01).
notes: Attention is limited: the ear follows 2-3 streams in focus; detail beyond that becomes texture. A budget keeps the peak sections peaky.
Before building: write the budget into the brief, check after each render.
composer density: mean layers per section inside the role target; suggestions "add" / "remove".
Every section at the same density (flat energy curve)
The intro already at drop density

examples.title: LAY-01 detail budget per section
examples.code:
atom("intro", { type: "mini", body: "<1 1 0 0 0 0>" })
atom("drop", { type: "mini", body: "<0 0 1 1 1 1>" })
$: s("bd*4").hook("hygiene-kick").mask(atoms.drop)
$: s("hh*8").hook("hygiene-hat").gain(0.4)
$: note("c2*8").s("sawtooth").hook("hygiene-bass").mask(atoms.drop)
$: chord("<Cm Ab>").voicing().s("supersaw").hook("hygiene-pad").gain(0.2).mask(atoms.intro)

sections.title: LAY-02 Layer ladder: core, support, ornament, atmos
sections.explain: Each layer gets a role: core (beat, bass, hook), support (chords, counterline), ornament (fills, one-shots), atmos (pads, noise, reverb beds).
notes: Roles make subtraction decisions easy (remove ornaments first, never the core) and keep the hierarchy readable.
Every arrangement; label lanes with tags so selections follow roles.
composer density: the "roles" map (core, support, ornament, atmos per layer) and the per-bar role counts.
Two core leads fighting for attention

examples.title: LAY-02 layer ladder: core, support, ornament, atmos
examples.code:
kick: s("bd*4").hook("hygiene-kick").tags("core")
bass: note("c2*8").s("sawtooth").hook("hygiene-bass").tags("core")
keys: chord("<Cm Ab>").voicing().s("triangle").hook("hygiene-keys").tags("support")
fill: s("~ ~ ~ sd*4").hook("hygiene-snare").tags("ornament").mask("<0 0 0 1>")
air: s("pink").hpf(6000).gain(0.05).tags("atmos")
tagged("ornament | atmos").mute("<2b")
examples.lowered_note: lane tags and selections (.tags, tagged().mute / solo / fx) choose events by lane while the program plays, through the Craft lane engine; plain Strudel has no tags or selections

sections.title: LAY-03 Simultaneous layer counts per genre and section
sections.explain: Target ranges of simultaneous lanes (each drum piece counts) per section role, scaled per genre.
notes: Producer-reported norms (COMPOSITION_RESEARCH.md): drops are the fullest section, cloud and riddim stay sparse, big-room and DnB carry more. Design call: intro 2-6, verse 4-9, build 5-10, drop 8-14, breakdown 3-7, outro 2-6 lanes; genre factor cloud 0.6, riddim 0.75, trap 0.85, phonk 0.9, house / dubstep / DnB 1.0, big room 1.1.
Planning and checking; override the factor with --genre.
composer density --genre G: section means against the scaled targets.
Treating the numbers as rules (they are conventions; the brief wins)

examples.title: LAY-03 simultaneous layer counts per genre and section
examples.code:
// the targets live in engine/composer/density.py (TARGETS, GENRE); a sparse riddim drop:
$: s("bd ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~, ~ ~ ~ ~ sd ~ ~ ~").hook("hygiene-kick")
$: s("hh*8").hook("hygiene-hat").gain(0.3)
$: note("c1 ~ ~ c1 ~ ~ c1 ~").s("sine").hook("hygiene-sub")
$: note("c2 ~ ~ c2 ~ ~ c2 ~").s("sawtooth").hook("hygiene-growl").lpf(sine.fast(2).range(300, 1500))
examples.lowered:
// the targets live in engine/composer/density.py (TARGETS, GENRE); a sparse riddim drop:
$: s("bd ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~, ~ ~ ~ ~ sd ~ ~ ~").hpf(30).lpf(7000)
$: s("hh*8").hpf(5000).lpf(14500).ftype("24db").gain(0.3)
$: note("c1 ~ ~ c1 ~ ~ c1 ~").s("sine").hpf(25)
$: note("c2 ~ ~ c2 ~ ~ c2 ~").s("sawtooth").hpf(70).lpf(9000).lpf(sine.fast(2).range(300, 1500))

sections.title: LAY-04 Frequency-slot allocation
sections.explain: Each layer owns a band (sub, bass, low-mid, mid, high-mid, presence, air); at most one owner in sub and two in bass.
notes: Simultaneous masking is strongest within a critical band: two sounds in one slot blur; in different slots both stay clear.
Sound selection and octave choice before EQ; carve with hpf/lpf after.
composer density: "slot" suggestions (sub shared by > 1, bass by > 2 layers); composer layers masking_risk; composer scan band map.
Two layers in the sub band without ducking (SYN-01)
Every layer full range (no slot left)

sections.title: LAY-05 Embellishment ladder per repeat
sections.explain: Each repeat of a loop adds or changes one small thing: repeat 1 plain, 2 + ornament, 3 + counter-rhythm, 4 + fill.
notes: Exact repetition habituates within 2-4 cycles; one change per repeat keeps attention while the loop identity stays.
Every 8-16 bar loop in drops and verses.
composer density: no "embellish" suggestion (same active set for >= 8 bars).
Changing the hook itself on every repeat

sections.title: LAY-06 Ear-candy cadence
sections.explain: Small one-shots (reverse cymbal, vocal chop, delay throw, riser) placed at phrase marks: every 4, 8 or 16 bars.
notes: Phrase boundaries are where attention resets; a marker there confirms the grid and rewards listening (producer-reported: once per 8 bars).
Drops and verses; fewer in intros (DJ mixing room).
composer density: ornament-role layers have onsets every 4-8 bars; no "embellish" suggestion.
Ear candy on every bar (it becomes texture)

sections.title: LAY-07 Detail by register
sections.explain: Busy parts high, slow parts low: the bass moves least, the top moves most.
notes: Low frequencies need longer to be resolved (fewer cycles per note) and mask more; fast detail is clear only in the highs.
Writing parts: check note rates per band.
composer density + ledger: onset rate per band (sub and bass lanes lowest).

examples.title: LAY-07 detail by register
examples.code:
$: note("c1 ~ ~ ~ c1 ~ ~ ~").s("sine").hook("hygiene-sub")
$: note("c3 ~ eb3 ~").s("sawtooth").hook("hygiene-keys")
$: note("c5 eb5 g5 bb5 c6 bb5 g5 eb5").s("triangle").hook("hygiene-arp").gain(0.3)
examples.lowered:
$: note("c1 ~ ~ ~ c1 ~ ~ ~").s("sine").hpf(25)
$: note("c3 ~ eb3 ~").s("sawtooth").hpf(80).lpf(7000)
$: note("c5 eb5 g5 bb5 c6 bb5 g5 eb5").s("triangle").hpf(150).lpf(8000).gain(0.3)

sections.title: LAY-08 Contrast by subtraction
sections.explain: Energy by removing layers before an arrival: a drop-out bar, a beat of silence, the kick gone for the last bar of the build.
notes: Loudness and density are judged relative to what came before (adaptation); a gap makes the return feel larger than adding more would.
The bar or beat before each drop; inside drops every 8-16 bars.
composer density: no "subtract" suggestion before drops; the curve dips in the bar before a drop.
Subtracting the hook (subtract support and ornaments first)

sections.title: TEN-01 Harmonic tension
sections.explain: Dominant function, leading tones, suspensions and non-chord tones that want to move.
notes: Tonal expectation: unstable degrees (7, 4, b2) predict motion to stable ones (1, 3, 5); delaying it holds tension.
composer discord: the leading tone (raised 7) named in the pre-drop section; roughness peak resolved on the drop downbeat.
A dominant that never resolves anywhere in the track

sections.title: TEN-02 Rhythmic tension
sections.explain: Subdivision acceleration: snare 1/4 -> 1/8 -> 1/16 -> 1/32 rolls, hats doubling, ratchets.
notes: Increasing event rate raises arousal and predicts an endpoint (the downbeat).
The last 2-8 bars of a build.
composer density: onsets per bar rising through the build; composer cluster: build bars in their own cluster.
Rolls that run into the drop downbeat (the gap is lost)

sections.title: TEN-03 Spectral tension
sections.explain: Brightness rises before the arrival: high-pass rising on the mix, low-pass opening on leads, noise risers.
notes: Spectral centroid correlates with perceived tension and energy; removing lows (HPF) makes the return of the low end the release.
Builds; the whole mix or the music bus, not the kick alone.
composer scan: band map shows sub and bass falling, presence rising across the build; centroid up.
Masking production moves because they sound "EDM": risers and filter builds are tools in any genre (user directive)

sections.title: TEN-04 Dynamic tension: the gap
sections.explain: Silence or near-silence (a beat or a bar) immediately before the drop.
notes: A gap resets loudness adaptation and creates maximal temporal expectation of the downbeat.
Before drops; before a beat switch.
composer density: the last bar before a drop has fewer layers (no "subtract" suggestion).
A gap with a reverb tail filling it completely

sections.title: TEN-05 Release grammar
sections.explain: What happens on the arrival downbeat: impact, sub returns, hook enters, filter fully open, crash.
notes: Several cues landing together (cross-modal: low end, brightness, loudness, hook) make the arrival unambiguous.
composer cluster: the drop starts a new cluster on its first bar; composer density: the curve jumps at the drop bar.
Staggered entries after the downbeat that blur the arrival (unless intended: then make it a pattern)

sections.title: EN-01 Macro energy arc
sections.explain: An energy level 1-10 per section written before building: e.g. intro 3, build 5, drop 9, break 4, build 6, drop 10, outro 3.
notes: Contrast between sections drives interest; the second peak higher than the first rewards staying.
The brief; the density budget derives from it (LAY-01).
composer density curve and composer scan band map follow the planned arc; the last drop >= the first.
The highest point in the first 30 seconds

sections.title: EN-02 Phrase ramp
sections.explain: Inside a 8 or 16-bar section, energy rises toward the phrase end (fills, opening filter, added hats).
notes: Phrase-level expectation: the end of a hypermetric unit is where change is expected.
Every section that leads into another.
composer density: within-section layer count or onset count rises to the last bar.
Every phrase ending with the same fill (habituates)

sections.title: EN-03 False drop
sections.explain: The build leads to an expected drop, but a different, sparser section (or a second build) arrives instead.
notes: Violated expectation is surprising and makes the real drop that follows stronger.
Second build; once per track at most.
composer cluster: the bar after the build belongs to a breakdown-like cluster, the following one to the drop cluster.
False drops twice in one track

sections.title: TR-01 Pickup fill
sections.explain: A short fill in the last beat(s) before the new section (snare, toms, 808 slide).
notes: Anacrusis: the upbeat points at the downbeat and connects the sections.
Every section change; vary the fill per occurrence.
composer density: an ornament-role onset in the last beat of each section.
The same fill before every section

sections.title: TR-02 Riser and impact
sections.explain: A riser that ends exactly on the downbeat, an impact that starts on it (dt.rise / dt.hit).
notes: Continuous pitch / noise rise predicts an endpoint; the impact confirms it.
Builds into drops, section changes in cinematic and EDM forms (and any genre that wants them).
composer scan: presence band rising over the build bars, a broadband onset on the drop bar.
A riser that stops before the downbeat (dead air) or overruns it

sections.title: TR-03 Drop-out bar
sections.explain: All or most layers stop for the bar or beat before the new section (see TEN-04).
notes: Contrast by subtraction at the seam.
composer density: dip in the last bar of the section.

sections.title: TR-04 Reverse swell
sections.explain: A reversed tail (reverse cymbal, reversed chord) ending on the downbeat.
notes: An amplitude envelope rising into the downbeat is an inverted decay: it reads as anticipation.
Into drops and choruses; into a vocal entry.
composer scan: energy rising through the last bar, ending at the downbeat.
A swell that ends after the downbeat

sections.title: TR-05 Overlap tail and crossfade
sections.explain: A layer of the old section rings into the new one, or two layers cross-fade over a bar.
notes: Continuity across the seam: the ear follows the overlapping element through the change.
Breakdowns into drops (pad tail), section changes in house and DnB.
composer density: the old layer active in the first bar of the new section.
Long tails in the low band across a drop (mud on the downbeat)

sections.title: TR-06 Delay throw
sections.explain: One word or note sent to a long delay at a phrase end; the echoes bridge the gap.
notes: Echoes keep the last event alive across silence, connecting phrases.
Phrase ends, before drops, vocal tags.
composer scan: energy continuing in the mid band through the gap bar.

sections.title: TR-07 Turnaround
sections.explain: The last bar of a loop changes chord or riff so the loop "turns" back to the start.
notes: Harmonic rhythm acceleration at the cycle end marks the boundary and drives back to bar 1.
composer discord: a chord change in the last bar of each loop; composer cluster: the turnaround bar forms its own small cluster.

sections.title: GRV-01 Rhythm sequence archetypes
sections.explain: Named drum skeletons: four-on-the-floor (house, big room), two-step (DnB), half-time (dubstep, trap, phonk), boom-bap, tresillo 3+3+2, electro broken kick, hyphy bounce.
notes: Each archetype sets the metric hierarchy listeners dance to; genre recognition starts from it.
Pick one per section; a beat switch changes it (ARR-04).
composer scan / feel: modal onset pattern, half-time flag, syncopation index.
Mixing two archetypes in one section by accident (ambiguous downbeat)

examples.title: GRV-01 rhythm sequence archetypes
examples.code:
$: s("bd*4, ~ cp ~ cp, [~ hh]*4").hook("hygiene-kick")  // four-floor
$: s("bd ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ bd ~ ~ ~ ~ ~, ~ ~ ~ ~ sd ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ sd ~ ~ ~").hook("hygiene-kick").mask("<0 1>")  // two-step

sections.title: GRV-02 Swing
sections.explain: The second 16th (or 8th) of each pair delayed: 50 % straight, 54-58 % pocket, 66.7 % triplet (pat.groove swing).
notes: Long-short pairs create lilt; small swing values are felt rather than heard.
Hip-hop, house hats, boom-bap; little or none in big room and riddim.
composer feel / scan: swing16 within 1-2 % of the target.
Two swings stacked (pat.groove and swingBy) (they compose)
Swinging the kick and not the hats (flam feel)

examples.title: GRV-02 swing
examples.code:
$: s("hh*16").hook("hygiene-hat").groove({ swing: 57, seed: 1 }).gain(0.4)
$: s("bd ~ ~ bd ~ ~ bd ~, ~ sd").hook("hygiene-kick")

lowered_check.reason: a groove (swing, push, humanize) is approximated in plain Strudel: it shifts onsets, not note lengths, and its random jitter is a different sequence (event 0 differs); with the groove taken out of both forms the events are identical

sections.title: GRV-03 Push and pull
sections.explain: A constant early (push, rush) or late (pull, drag) offset per voice, in % of a 16th.
notes: Relative timing between voices sets feel: late snares feel laid back, early hats urgent.
Pushing the whole mix (nothing changes relatively)

examples.title: GRV-03 push and pull
examples.code:
$: s("~ sd").hook("hygiene-snare").groove({ push: 8, seed: 2 })
$: s("bd ~ ~ bd").hook("hygiene-kick")

lowered_check.reason: a groove (swing, push, humanize) is approximated in plain Strudel: it shifts onsets, not note lengths, and its random jitter is a different sequence (event 1 differs); with the groove taken out of both forms the events are identical

sections.title: GRV-04 Micro-timing (humanize)
sections.explain: Small per-hit timing spread (jitter 1-5 % of a 16th) and slow drift, seeded and deterministic.
notes: Players deviate 5-20 ms; a little variance reads as alive, too much as sloppy.
Hats, percussion, keys; not the kick in four-floor genres.
composer feel / scan: jitter_pct16 within the feel template range.
Random jitter on the kick and sub (phase smear)

lowered_check.reason: a groove (swing, push, humanize) is approximated in plain Strudel: it shifts onsets, not note lengths, and its random jitter is a different sequence (event count differs (64 Craft, 63 Strudel)); with the groove taken out of both forms the events are identical

sections.title: GRV-05 Ghost notes
sections.explain: Quiet notes (velocity 0.1-0.35) between the main hits, mostly snare and hats.
notes: Ghosts fill the subdivision grid at low salience: the groove gets motion without changing its accents.
Boom-bap, DnB breaks, funk-derived house, phonk.
composer feel / scan: ghost_share and ghosts_per_bar.
Ghosts as loud as accents (they stop being ghosts)

examples.title: GRV-05 ghost notes
examples.code:
$: s("~ sd ~ sd").hook("hygiene-snare")
$: s("~ ~ ~ sd ~ ~ sd ~ ~ sd ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ sd").hook("hygiene-snare").velocity(0.22)

sections.title: GRV-06 Polymeter and hemiola
sections.explain: A cycle of 3 (or 6) against the 4 of the bar: a 3-step riff over 16ths, 3+3+2 groupings.
notes: Phase drift between cycles creates moving accents over a stable pulse (realigns every LCM steps).
Techno, DnB riffs, trap hats, builds.
composer scan / feel: hemiola_hint (autocorrelation at lag 3 or 6 beats lag 4 and 8).
Polymeter on the kick in a dance track (the floor loses the pulse)

sections.title: GRV-07 Picking a feel
sections.explain: Choose a feel template (feel-boombap, lazy, trap, hyphy, cloud, halftime, ukf, riddim, brostep) from measured or intended stats.
notes: A feel is a coherent set of tempo, archetype and groove settings; picking one keeps all voices consistent.
At the start, or from a reference you own: composer scan, then composer feel.
composer feel: ranked feels with distances; the measured .groove line.
Copying a reference track's pattern (measure feel stats, never transcribe or duplicate)

examples.title: GRV-07 picking a feel
examples.lowered:
setcpm(140/4)
$: s("<[x ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ x ~ ~ ~ ~ ~] [x ~ ~ x ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ x ~ ~ ~ x ~]>").velocity("1").hpf(30).lpf(7000).hpf(30).lpf(7000).s("sine").freq(55).penv(36).pdecay(0.04).decay(0.28).sustain(0).noise(0.12).shape(0.4).gain(0.8).hpf(40).mul(velocity(rand.late(1.37).range(0.82, 1))).late(rand.late(1).range(0, 0.001875).segment(16)).early(0.000938)

lowered_check.reason: a groove (swing, push, humanize) is approximated in plain Strudel: it shifts onsets, not note lengths, and its random jitter is a different sequence (event 0 differs); with the groove taken out of both forms the events are identical

sections.title: HAR-01 Voice leading
sections.explain: Chord changes with the smallest moves per voice; common tones held.
notes: Small moves keep voices as continuous streams; pads sound smooth instead of jumping.
engine/motifs chord loop; pitch moves per voice <= 2 semitones (voicing()).
Root-position block chords jumping a fifth each change

sections.title: HAR-02 Bass-note pedal
sections.explain: The bass holds one note while chords change above (I - IV/I - bVII/I).
notes: Inverted and slash chords over a pedal give tension and colour with a stable floor.
Intros, builds, phonk and techno drones.
composer discord: one bar root across chord changes; roughness changes per chord.
A pedal through a whole track with no release

sections.title: HAR-03 Harmonic rhythm
sections.explain: How often chords change: 1 per 2 bars (house, dubstep), 1 per bar (pop), 2 per bar (turnarounds).
notes: Faster harmonic rhythm raises energy and forward motion; slower lets texture and groove lead.
Accelerate into a drop or chorus, slow down in breakdowns.
composer discord / engine/motifs: chord changes per bar per section.
Changing harmonic rhythm under a vocal phrase mid-line

sections.title: HAR-04 Modal colour per genre
sections.explain: Pick the mode for its colour: Aeolian (most EDM), Dorian (house, liquid), Phrygian (phonk, darker dubstep), harmonic minor (Italo, trance tension).
notes: The characteristic degree (natural 6 in Dorian, b2 in Phrygian) carries the mood.
At the brief; borrowing (BOR) can mix modes per section.
composer discord: borrowing names b2 (Phrygian) or natural 6 (Dorian) against the minor key.
Phrygian b2 against a held natural 2 (unwanted clash)

sections.title: BOR-01 Modal interchange (borrowed chords)
sections.explain: A chord from the parallel mode inside the key: iv, bVI, bVII in major; IV, major V in minor.
notes: One altered degree (b6, b7, or a raised 6 / 7) changes colour without leaving the tonic (music theory: mode mixture).
Sentimental lifts, pre-choruses, last chords before a drop.
composer discord: borrowing lists b6 (mixture, bVI / iv) in that section.
Borrowing every bar (the key stops being clear)

sections.title: BOR-02 Parallel and relative shifts
sections.explain: A section in the parallel major/minor (C minor -> C major) or the relative key (C minor -> Eb major).
notes: Same tonic, opposite mode (parallel) or same notes, new centre (relative): big mood change with continuity.
composer discord: key_shift on the section (or major 3 "parallel major" named).
Shifting mode under a sustained vocal note that clashes

sections.title: BOR-03 Picardy third
sections.explain: A minor piece ends on a major tonic chord.
notes: The raised third surprises at the cadence and reads as release or hope.
Outros, the last chord of a breakdown.
composer discord: "major 3 (Picardy / parallel major)" in the last section.
Using it on every loop (it becomes the key)

sections.title: BOR-04 Chromatic mediants
sections.explain: Chords a third apart that share at most one tone (C major -> E major, Cm -> Ab with a major-third root move and borrowed quality).
notes: Large colour shift with smooth common-tone voice leading: cinematic and "lift" effect.
Section seams, trailer-like moments, melodic dubstep breakdowns.
Mediant shifts under a modal vocal melody

sections.title: BOR-05 Key-shift lift
sections.explain: The last chorus or drop moves up (often 1 or 2 semitones; a fourth or fifth for a broader lift).
notes: Raised pitch raises brightness and arousal; the familiar hook in a new key feels like a lift.
The final hook; once per track.
composer discord: key_shift with lift_semitones in the last drop; composer ledger: "transposed" statements there.
A lift without preparation (pivot chord or gap)

sections.title: BOR-06 Timbre borrowing
sections.explain: Take the timbre of one layer for another: neuro growl formants on a pad, a vocal formant on the bass, bell FM on a pluck.
notes: Shared spectral envelope across layers binds them (ASN) and makes a new colour from known material.
Drops of bass genres; breakdowns that reuse the drop's colour softly.
composer layers: shared vowel or high MFCC cosine (stems) between the two layers.
Borrowing a timbre into the same band (masking instead of binding)

sections.title: BOR-07 Groove and envelope borrowing
sections.explain: One layer takes another layer's rhythm or envelope (the hat rhythm on a pluck, the kick envelope on a pad via sidechain), or a genre feel on a new style.
notes: Shared onsets and envelopes lock layers into one groove (common fate).
Drops; genre blends (hyphy feel under a house chord).
composer layers: rhythm_rhyme / envelope_rhyme high for the pair.
Borrowing a groove that fights the main archetype

examples.title: BOR-07 groove and envelope borrowing
examples.code:
atom("hats", { type: "mini", body: "~ x ~ x ~ x ~ x" })
$: s("hh").struct(atoms.hats).hook("hygiene-hat").gain(0.4)
$: n("0 2 4 2").scale("C5:minor").struct(atoms.hats).s("triangle").hook("hygiene-pluck")
examples.lowered:
$: s("hh").struct("~ x ~ x ~ x ~ x").hpf(5000).lpf(14500).ftype("24db").gain(0.4)
$: n("0 2 4 2").scale("C5:minor").struct("~ x ~ x ~ x ~ x").s("triangle").hpf(120).lpf(7000)

sections.title: BOR-08 Harmonic skeleton borrowing
sections.explain: A section reuses another section's chord loop or bass skeleton with new material on top.
notes: Continuity of harmony makes contrasting melodies belong to one piece.
Breakdowns over the drop loop; verses over the hook chords.
composer foreshadow: planted_harmony; composer discord: same roots per bar in both sections.
Different loops in every section (no harmonic identity)

examples.title: BOR-08 harmonic skeleton borrowing
examples.code:
atom("loop", { type: "mini", body: "<Cm Ab Eb Bb>" })
$: chord(atoms.loop).voicing().s("supersaw").hook("hygiene-pad").gain(0.2).mask("<1 1 0 0>")
$: chord(atoms.loop).voicing().s("triangle").hook("hygiene-keys").struct("x ~ x x").mask("<0 0 1 1>")
examples.lowered:
$: chord("<Cm Ab Eb Bb>").voicing().s("supersaw").hpf(180).lpf(6000).gain(0.2).mask("<1 1 0 0>")
$: chord("<Cm Ab Eb Bb>").voicing().s("triangle").hpf(80).lpf(7000).struct("x ~ x x").mask("<0 0 1 1>")

sections.title: DIS-01 Minor-second and tritone stabs
sections.explain: Short stabs whose voicing contains a minor 2nd, major 7th or tritone.
notes: Partials within a critical band beat and roughen (Plomp-Levelt); short duration keeps the roughness a hit, not a texture.
Dark drops, industrial dubstep, phonk bells (the cowbell's near-tritone partials), horror tints.
composer discord: interval classes m2/M7, tritone in the section; roughness peaks on the stabs.
Sustained clashes under a vocal (unintended "out of tune")

sections.title: DIS-02 Cluster stabs
sections.explain: Three or more adjacent scale tones at once (c-d-eb), short.
notes: Maximum roughness per event; reads as a percussive, metallic hit.
composer discord: interval class "cluster"; roughness x2+ the section median on the hit bars.
Low clusters (below ~200 Hz: mud, not bite)

sections.title: DIS-03 Detuned unison beating
sections.explain: Two or more copies of a voice detuned by a few cents (supersaw, reese).
notes: Beating at the frequency difference gives motion and width; at low pitch it becomes audible pulsing.
Reese basses (DnB, neuro), supersaw chords; keep the sub itself clean.
composer discord: roughness counts detuned copies (unison, detune); composer layers stems: the sub stem stays clean (no beating under 60 Hz).
Detuning the sub (phase cancellation, mono collapse)

sections.title: DIS-04 Bitonal layers
sections.explain: Two layers in keys a tritone or semitone apart for a short span.
notes: Two tonal centres compete; the ear cannot settle: strong unease, best brief.
Horror tints, the last bars of an industrial build.
composer discord: per-section key fit drops; out-of-key share rises in that section only.
Bitonality for whole sections without intent

sections.title: DIS-05 Dissonance-to-resolution timing
sections.explain: Place the clash on a weak or pre-arrival position and resolve on the downbeat (appoggiatura logic).
notes: Tension then release; an unresolved clash reads as error, a resolved one as intent.
composer discord: every clash has resolved_at within 2 bars; unresolved list empty (or intended).
Clashes left hanging at section ends

sections.title: DIS-06 Roughness as sound design
sections.explain: Distortion, FM and ring-style sidebands that create inharmonic, rough spectra (wet industrial, growls).
notes: Inharmonic partials close together raise sensory roughness; it reads as aggression and grit.
Growl and riddim basses, industrial dubstep, phonk distortion; keep the sub separate.
composer discord --audio on the stem: roughness per bar; composer scan band map: grit above 200 Hz, a clean sub band.
Distorting the sub with the growl (one band split first, SND-02)

sections.title: ASN-01 Shared vowel formants
sections.explain: Two layers filtered to the same vowel (bass and vocal syllables both on "o").
notes: Formants are the strongest cue for sound similarity in voice-like sounds; shared formants bind layers into one colour.
Talking basses with vocal chops, formant pads with leads.
composer layers: colour "shared vowel" for the pair; stems: high MFCC cosine.

sections.title: ASN-02 Shared harmonic series
sections.explain: Layers placed on partials of one fundamental (octaves, fifths over the bass root).
notes: Harmonic partials fuse (harmonicity): the layers sound like one rich tone.
Pads over a sub, drones, bell layers.
composer discord: low roughness with many voices; composer layers stems: lufs_gain_db >= 0 (no cancellation).
Tempered thirds high above a sub expecting perfect fusion (slight beating is normal)

sections.title: ASN-03 Repeated colour and noise texture
sections.explain: One noise colour (vinyl, tape hiss, pink air) or one reverb space shared by several layers.
notes: A common acoustic signature (same room, same noise floor) makes separate sources sound recorded together.
Lo-fi, phonk, cloud; any mix that feels disjointed.
composer layers: same room / filter colour; composer scan: a constant noise floor in the brilliance band.
Noise so loud it masks transients

examples.title: ASN-03 repeated colour and noise texture

sections.title: ASN-04 Rhyming rhythm cells
sections.explain: Two layers share a rhythm cell (same onsets) with different pitches or sounds.
notes: Shared onsets group layers by common fate; the groove gets one identity.
Drops: bass and stab, kick and sub, chord stabs and hats.
composer layers: rhythm_rhyme close to 1 for the pair.
Every layer on the same cell (no complement left, see CMP-02)

examples.title: ASN-04 rhyming rhythm cells
examples.code:
atom("cell", { type: "mini", body: "x ~ x ~ ~ x ~ x" })
$: note("c2").struct(atoms.cell).s("sawtooth").hook("hygiene-bass")
$: chord("Cm").voicing().struct(atoms.cell).s("square").hook("hygiene-stab").decay(0.1).sustain(0)
examples.lowered:
$: note("c2").struct("x ~ x ~ ~ x ~ x").s("sawtooth").hpf(40).lpf(3500)
$: chord("Cm").voicing().struct("x ~ x ~ ~ x ~ x").s("square").hpf(120).lpf(8000).decay(0.1).sustain(0)

sections.title: ASN-05 Rhyming envelopes
sections.explain: Layers share an attack/decay shape (all plucky, or all swelling).
notes: Envelope shape is a primary timbre cue; matching envelopes make layers belong to one gesture.
Pluck layers, stab stacks, pad beds.
One slow-attack layer inside a pluck stack (smears the transient)

sections.title: ASN-06 Onset alliteration
sections.explain: Several layers start together on chosen beats (accents everyone hits), then separate.
notes: Coincident onsets are heard as one accent: hits get weight; the rest of the bar stays clear.
Accents on 1 and the "and of 2" in hip-hop; drop downbeats.
composer layers: onset_lock above chance for the accent layers.
Everything on every accent (flams if timing differs)

examples.title: ASN-06 onset alliteration
examples.code:
$: s("bd ~ ~ bd ~ ~ ~ ~").hook("hygiene-kick")
$: note("c2 ~ ~ c2 ~ eb2 ~ ~").s("sawtooth").hook("hygiene-bass")
$: chord("Cm").voicing().struct("x ~ ~ x ~ ~ ~ ~").s("square").hook("hygiene-stab").decay(0.1).sustain(0)
examples.lowered:
$: s("bd ~ ~ bd ~ ~ ~ ~").hpf(30).lpf(7000)
$: note("c2 ~ ~ c2 ~ eb2 ~ ~").s("sawtooth").hpf(40).lpf(3500)
$: chord("Cm").voicing().struct("x ~ ~ x ~ ~ ~ ~").s("square").hpf(120).lpf(8000).decay(0.1).sustain(0)

sections.title: CMP-01 Spectral complement and mask-aware carving
sections.explain: Layers that compete get mirrored filtering: where one is boosted, the other is cut (or high/low-passed apart).
notes: Masking is band-local: removing overlap gives each layer its own critical bands (producer-reported "puzzle-piece" EQ).
Kick vs bass, vocal vs lead, pads vs keys.
composer layers (stems): masking_index falls after carving; composer density: no slot suggestions.
Carving so deep a layer sounds hollow solo and in context

examples.title: CMP-01 spectral complement and mask-aware carving

sections.title: CMP-02 Rhythmic complement
sections.explain: Onbeat vs offbeat, notes in the other layer's rests (the offbeat bass in house, hats between kicks).
notes: Interleaved onsets give a denser composite rhythm with no masking in time.
Bass vs kick, chops vs snare, counterlines.
composer layers: onset_complement close to 1 and "best complement" for each layer.
Complement so strict both layers sound like one choppy part

examples.title: CMP-02 rhythmic complement
examples.code:
$: s("bd*4").hook("hygiene-kick")
$: note("~ c2 ~ c2 ~ c2 ~ c2").s("sawtooth").hook("hygiene-bass")

sections.title: CMP-03 Sustained vs staccato
sections.explain: Long notes against short ones: pad against plucks, held bass against stabs.
notes: Different envelopes separate into streams and fill both the time and the spectrum.
Any two melodic layers that share a register.
composer layers: length_contrast >= 2 (log2 ratio of median durations).

sections.title: CMP-04 Stereo complement
sections.explain: Mono low end and lead; width in pads, hats, reverbs; panned pairs left/right.
notes: Spatial separation releases masking (binaural unmasking) and mono lows stay solid on any system.
Always: bass and kick mono, supporting layers wide.
composer layers: pan_contrast; stems: low-band correlation stays mono.

sections.title: CMP-05 Dynamic complement (ducking)
sections.explain: One layer gets quieter while another plays (sidechain, ducking on a bus).
notes: Time-varying gain separates layers in loudness when they must share a band.
Kick and sub, vocal and pads, impacts and the mix.
composer density: the sub slot shared by a ducked pair is not flagged; stems: kick transients clear.
Pumping everything (the groove becomes the compressor)

sections.title: SYN-01 Kick and sub lock
sections.explain: The kick's pitch and decay tuned with the sub: same root, the sub ducked or starting after the kick transient.
notes: In phase and in tune the two sum into one low event; out of phase they cancel (comb filtering at the overlap).
Every genre with a separate kick and sub (trap 808 + kick, dubstep, DnB).
composer layers (stems): lufs_gain_db >= 0 for kick + sub (no cancellation); events: onset_lock over chance.
Kick and sub a semitone apart
No ducking and long sub tails under every kick

sections.title: SYN-02 Bass and pad reinforcement
sections.explain: The pad voices sit on the bass note's partials (octave, fifth, tenth), so together they make one chord-tone.
notes: Harmonic reinforcement raises loudness of shared partials and fuses the two.
Breakdowns and drops with sustained chords.
Pad thirds in the bass octave

sections.title: SYN-03 Snare and noise tail
sections.explain: A tonal snare body and a noise layer that only work together (body + tail).
notes: Transient, body and decay come from different layers; each alone is thin, together they make one snare.
Snares and claps in every genre.
composer layers: onset_lock 1.0 for the pair, different bands.

sections.title: SYN-04 Vocal formant and lead filter sweep
sections.explain: The lead's filter sweeps through the same region as the vocal's formants, alternating in time.
notes: Shared spectral region in alternation reads as a duet of one colour.
Hooks with vocal chops and a synth lead.
composer layers: filter centres within 1/2 octave and onset_complement high.
Sweeping through the vocal while it sings

examples.title: SYN-04 vocal formant and lead filter sweep

sections.title: SYN-05 Sidechain interplay
sections.explain: The kick ducks pads and bass so the pumping becomes part of the groove.
notes: Amplitude modulation at the beat rate synchronises layers to the kick (common fate).
House, big room, French house filter loops, phonk drops.
composer scan: low-band onset pattern on every beat and pad energy dips between; composer density ducks recognised.
Masking sidechain because it is "EDM": it is a tool for any genre (user directive)

sections.title: CLU-01 Tone clusters
sections.explain: Adjacent tones sounded together (seconds), as colour (soft, high) or as attack (loud, short).
notes: High soft clusters shimmer (beating as texture); loud clusters are percussive roughness.
composer discord: "cluster" interval class; roughness level vs section median.
Mid-low clusters held under a vocal

sections.title: CLU-02 Chord clusters (dense voicings)
sections.explain: Add9, sus2, 6/9 and 11 voicings with seconds inside, spread above 200 Hz.
notes: Seconds inside open voicings add colour (the "bittersweet" melodic-bass sound) without the roughness of close low clusters.
Melodic dubstep and future bass chords, liquid DnB pads.
composer discord: m2/M7 present with moderate roughness (no clash flag).

sections.title: CLU-03 Rhythmic clusters
sections.explain: Bursts of events in a short span: flams, ratchets, drags, rolls.
notes: A burst is heard as one ornamented event: emphasis and swing within a beat.
composer feel: ghost and onset counts per bar; rhythm cells with subdivisions in the ledger rhythm list.

sections.title: CLU-04 Event clustering over time
sections.explain: Density bursts at points: more events just before the drop, sparse elsewhere.
notes: Time-varying density shapes expectation; bursts point at arrivals.
The last 1-2 bars of builds, the bar before a switch.
composer density: onsets per bar peak at the end of the build.

sections.title: CLU-05 Bar clustering (analysis)
sections.explain: k-means over per-bar features (band energies, centroid, flatness, onsets or lane activation) finds section types without a form.
notes: Bars that sound alike cluster together; the run lengths reveal the form, turnaround bars and transition bars.
Audio you own (find its form), or a draft (did the drop really change?).
composer cluster: labels, runs, adjusted Rand index against the form.
Reading clusters as genre rules: they describe one track

examples.title: CLU-05 bar clustering (analysis)
examples.code:
// engine/composer/run.sh cluster MIX.wav OUT --bpm 128 [--form form.json]
$: s("bd*4, hh*8").hook("hygiene-kick").mask("<1 1 0 0 1 1>")
examples.lowered:
// engine/composer/run.sh cluster MIX.wav OUT --bpm 128 [--form form.json]
$: s("bd*4, hh*8").hpf(30).lpf(7000).mask("<1 1 0 0 1 1>")

sections.title: CLU-06 Motif clustering by contour
sections.explain: Group motif cells by their up/down contour to find families of related ideas.
notes: Contour is the most robust identity cue; cells sharing it sound related even with different intervals.
After drafting: are the motifs one family (unity) or unrelated (patchwork)?
Too many unrelated contours in one track

examples.title: CLU-06 motif clustering by contour
examples.code:
// engine/composer/run.sh ledger PROGRAM.strudel.js OUT -> contour_families
$: n("<[0 2 4 3] [0 3 5 4]>").scale("C4:minor").s("triangle").hook("hygiene-pluck")
examples.lowered:
// engine/composer/run.sh ledger PROGRAM.strudel.js OUT -> contour_families
$: n("<[0 2 4 3] [0 3 5 4]>").scale("C4:minor").s("triangle").hpf(120).lpf(7000)

sections.title: CLU-07 Timbral clustering
sections.explain: Group sounds into a few timbral families (metallic, airy, woody, distorted) and assign families to sections.
notes: A limited palette per section reads as intent; switching families marks sections.
composer layers (stems): MFCC cosine groups; composer cluster on stems.
Every layer a different family (no palette)

sections.title: SND-01 Sub, body, bite, air
sections.explain: One instrument from four layers: sub (sine, mono, < 100 Hz), body (100-500 Hz), bite (1-5 kHz transient or grit), air (> 8 kHz noise).
notes: Each band carries a different cue (weight, warmth, presence, sheen); separate layers allow separate processing and mono / stereo choices.
Basses, leads and snares that must translate on small and large systems.
composer scan band map: one layer dominant per band; composer layers stems: low masking between the layers.
Every layer full range (phase mush in the lows)

sections.title: SND-02 Parallel processing and band split
sections.explain: Process a copy in parallel (distortion, compression) or split by band (.split) so the sub stays clean.
notes: The low band keeps its phase and weight; the high band can be wrecked for character.
composer scan: sub band stays tonal (clean) while upper bands show grit; composer discord audio roughness above 200 Hz only.
Distorting the full band and then EQ-ing the sub back

examples.title: SND-02 parallel processing and band split
examples.lowered_note: splits, sends and returns (.split, .merge, .send, ret) are compiled by the Craft lane engine to audio buses with the source rendered once; strudel.cc has no buses

sections.title: SND-03 Serial chain order
sections.explain: The order of processes decides the sound: filter then distort (rounded grit) vs distort then filter (tamed harmonics).
notes: Non-linear stages generate harmonics from what reaches them; order sets which partials exist.
composer scan: the two orders give different band maps (A/B in one render).

sections.title: SND-04 Resampling and freezing
sections.explain: Render a processed sound to audio (capture), then rework it as a sample: chop, pitch, process again.
notes: Freezing modulation into a sample makes it consistent per note and opens new processing (producer-reported central in neurofunk).
the capture exists (CAPTURE.md); composer layers stems on the resampled layer.
Resampling forever without committing a palette

examples.title: SND-04 resampling and freezing
examples.code:
// strudel capture IN --name growl -o growl.wav (docs/CAPTURE.md), then use the capture as a sample
$: note("c2*4").s("sawtooth").hook("hygiene-growl").fm(2).distort(2)
examples.lowered:
// strudel capture IN --name growl -o growl.wav (docs/CAPTURE.md), then use the capture as a sample
$: note("c2*4").s("sawtooth").hpf(70).lpf(9000).fm(2).distort(2)

sections.title: VOX-01 Pitched syllables and vowels
sections.explain: Vowels or syllables as notes, no words: a melodic instrument with a voice colour.
notes: Voice-like spectra (formants) draw attention; without words they stay instrumental.
Hooks, breakdowns, phonk and melodic bass chops. Never add words the user did not write.
composer ledger: the motif on the vox lane; composer layers: shared vowel with another layer.
Inferring lyrics, crowd or choir parts the user did not ask for

sections.title: VOX-02 Sustained formant pad
sections.explain: A long vowel (formant filter or sustained sung vowel) as a pad layer.
notes: A vowel pad is warm and human and sits in the vocal band only lightly when filtered.
composer density: atmos role; composer layers: complement with the lead (length contrast).
A loud vowel pad under a lead vocal (masking in 300 Hz-3 kHz)

sections.title: VOX-03 Woven chops
sections.explain: Short vocal slices placed in the gaps of the groove (offbeats, after the snare), pitched to the chords.
notes: Short, pitched chops act as rhythmic ear candy and a call-and-response voice.
Drops of melodic bass, house, phonk; the user's own or licensed vocals only.
composer layers: onset_complement with the snare lane high.
Chopping vocals from other artists' tracks (never rip; the user's own or licensed material only)

sections.title: ARR-01 Forms as gates
sections.explain: One form map as gate atoms (intro, build, drop ...); lanes are selected by gate, never copied per section.
notes: One source of truth for the arrangement: changing a section length moves every layer.
composer density / cluster with --form: the gates match the cluster runs.

examples.title: ARR-01 forms as gates
examples.code:
atom("intro", { type: "gate", body: "<3b" })
atom("drop", { type: "gate", body: "@3b" })
kick: s("bd*4").hook("hygiene-kick").tags("drums")
pad: chord("<Cm Ab>").voicing().s("supersaw").hook("hygiene-pad").gain(0.2).tags("pad")
tagged("drums").mute(atoms.intro)
examples.lowered_note: lane tags and selections (.tags, tagged().mute / solo / fx) choose events by lane while the program plays, through the Craft lane engine; plain Strudel has no tags or selections

sections.title: ARR-02 Genre section maps
sections.explain: Typical bar maps: house intro 16-32, breakdown 16-32, drop 32; DnB DJ intro 32, drop 32-48 (16 main, 16 variation, roll-out); dubstep intro 16-32, build 8, drop 16-32, switch-up second drop; trap hook 8 / verse 16; big room build 16 with 8-bar riser, drop 32.
notes: Producer-reported conventions (COMPOSITION_RESEARCH.md); DJ mixing needs predictable phrase lengths in 8s.
Planning the form; a brief may override.
composer cluster: run lengths in multiples of 8; composer density per section.
Odd phrase lengths in a DJ tool without intent

examples.title: ARR-02 genre section maps
examples.code:
// 18 bars at 1 cycle per bar: intro 4, build 2, drop 4, break 2, build 2, drop 4 (scale x8 for a real 144-bar map)
atom("drops", { type: "mini", body: "<0!6 1!4 0!4 1!4>" })
atom("builds", { type: "mini", body: "<0!4 1!2 0!6 1!2 0!4>" })
$: s("bd*4").hook("hygiene-kick").mask(atoms.drops)
$: s("sd*8").hook("hygiene-snare").gain(0.4).mask(atoms.builds)

sections.title: ARR-03 DJ-friendly intro and outro
sections.explain: Drums-led 16-32 bar intro and outro with no full harmony, so DJs can mix.
notes: Beat-matched mixing needs a rhythm-only overlap; harmonic clashes between two tracks are avoided.
Club tracks (house, DnB, techno); not for listening edits.
composer density: intro and outro layers mostly drum role; composer discord: no harmony in the first bars.
Full chords from bar 1 in a club tool

sections.title: ARR-04 Switch-up second drop
sections.explain: The second drop keeps the hook but changes the beat, bass pattern or sound (beat switch, half/double time).
notes: Repetition with a twist: identity plus novelty, the main reward of the second drop.
composer cluster: the second drop is a different cluster from the first; composer ledger: the hook motif present in both.
A second drop identical to the first
A switch-up that drops the hook entirely

examples.title: ARR-04 switch-up second drop
examples.code:
atom("sw", { type: "gate", body: "@3b" })
hooks.bind("bass", [["lpf", 900]], "<3b")
hooks.bind("bass", [["lpf", 2500], ["distort", 1.5]], atoms.sw)
$: note("c2 ~ c2 eb2").s("sawtooth").hook("hygiene-bass").use("bass")
examples.lowered_note: the binding is gated (it opens at a bar or in a range): gates are evaluated by the Craft runtime as the song plays, plain Strudel has no timeline of bindings
